notation: FACT as in checkpoint-02: a direct factorization A+B=Z_n with A0={0,3,8,11} in A and B0={0,1,7,13,14} in B. Div(E)={gcd(e-e',n)}. R1 is Sands 1979 Thm3 (named import, as quoted by Dai 2026 Thm2.2). R5 is residue invariance. The size facts |A| even and 330 | |B| come from checkpoint-01 (A) (RSS89/PR plus Tijdeman multipliers, named imports).
class_SZ_definition: A pair (P,Q') is in class SZ if all of the following hold. (1) For some coprime CRT split Z_n = prod_i Z_{m_i} (i=1..r) and divisors d_i>=2 of m_i, P = prod_i P_i with each P_i a complete residue system mod d_i. (2) Q' = Q - q0 with q0 in Q, where Q = (H minus union C_j) union (union (C_j+g_j)). (3) H = prod_i d_i Z_{m_i} is the standard lattice complement. (4) The C_j are pairwise DISJOINT subsets of H, each a coset of one component lattice K_{i(j)} = d_{i(j)} Z_{m_{i(j)}}. (5) Each g_j lies in the same component group Z_{m_{i(j)}}. Such moves preserve P+Q=Z_n, because P_i+K_i = Z_{m_i}. This formalizes Szabo's 1985 construction, as described by Lagarias-Szabo 2001 (the Z_900 example has exactly three disjoint single-component coset moves, checked by hand). It also covers Dai 2026 Definition1.1 Szabo pairs, whose translated B lies in qrZ, rpZ and pqZ. Key property: every element of Q is off the lattice in AT MOST ONE CRT component, where off-lattice in i means component value not 0 mod d_i.

R6_theorem.statement: WRITTEN. No FACT solution lies in class SZ, in either orientation, and this stays true after any automorphism x->ux of Z_n.
R6_theorem.orientation_alpha: Take P = FACT-A and Q' = FACT-B, which contains 0 and 1, so Q contains q0 and q0+1. The element 1 (likewise any unit u) is off-lattice in every component, since d_i>=2. (A component with d_i=1 would force m_i | 3,8,11, so m_i=1.) So q0+1 is off-lattice in every component where q0 is on-lattice, which is at least r-1 of them. Hence r<=2. For r=2, every K_1-coset of H meets every K_2-coset of H at one point. Disjointness therefore allows only ONE move type, so all off-lattice elements of Q are off in the same component. But q0 and q0+1 are off in different components, or q0+1 is off in both. Contradiction. For r=1, Q is a translate of H, so FACT-B would be the subgroup d_1 Z_n, which contains 1. Then d_1=1, a contradiction.
R6_theorem.orientation_beta: Take P = FACT-B and Q' = FACT-A, so q0+y lies in Q for y in {0,3,8,11}. Let S_i = {y : q0+y on-lattice in component i}. Its elements are pairwise congruent mod e_i:=d_i. Every 3-subset of {0,3,8,11} has difference gcd 1, so |S_i|<=2. Each y is off in at most one component, so sum |S_i| >= 4(r-1) while sum |S_i| <= 2r. Hence r<=2. For r=2, the S_i partition {0,3,8,11} into pairs with e_i dividing the pair differences, and the m_i must be coprime. Pairs {0,3},{8,11} force two components divisible by 3. Pairs {0,8},{3,11} force two even components. Only {0,11},{3,8} remains, with e={11,5}. Then |FACT-B| = |P| = 55, which is not divisible by 330. For r=1, Q is a translate of H, so FACT-A is a subgroup containing 3 and 8, i.e. all of Z_n. Contradiction.
R6_theorem.automorphism_invariance: Replacing A0 and B0 by uA0 and uB0 for a unit u changes nothing above. Lattice membership depends only on divisibility by d_i, and u is prime to every d_i.
R6_theorem.scope: This is a route-control theorem about the known family. It does not exclude nested or multi-level coset-shift complements or any other non-SZ factorization.

R7_conditional_reduction.statement: CONDITIONAL, NOT a substitute for the quantifier. Hypothesis: every factorization of a finite cyclic group with 0 in both factors and neither factor in a proper subgroup (a Sands-conjecture counterexample) is in class SZ, up to automorphism and factor translation. Under it, R2 plus R6 give not-FACT. Hence no finite UD factor-complete superset of C exists, by the written PR interface (v2 section 2) or RSS89.
R7_conditional_reduction.hypothesis_status: OPEN. Dai 2026 section1.2 writes that 'no example essentially different from Szabo's has been found to date' and that it is 'natural to conjecture' that Szabo's construction is the only failure of Sands' conjecture. He PROVES the classification only for M=(pqr)^2 with |A|=|B|=pqr, which FACT cannot meet because 330 | |B|. My class SZ is one formalization of 'Szabo's construction'; Dai's wording is informal for general n.
R7_conditional_reduction.converse_reading: Any FACT witness, and hence any finite completion of Shor's code, would be a genuinely new type of Sands-conjecture counterexample, outside every currently known construction family. That is a precise measure of what the positive route would need.

first_unproved_original_step: Unchanged in kind, sharper in content. Decide FACT. Negative route: either prove not-FACT directly, or prove the R7 hypothesis for all n in 1320Z with |A|>=6 (open). Positive route: construct a non-SZ Sands counterexample containing A0 and B0, for example by nested coset-shift moves; R6 does not exclude these. Then the v2 joint-delay and all-arity bridge obligations remain.
next_action: Test whether NESTED moves (shifting a coset of a multi-component lattice by an element of the matching multi-component group, then moving inside it) can meet the Div constraint. In orientation alpha, R1 forces a component carrying 2,3,5,11 with no unit differences in its product factor. Either find a nested witness pattern or extend R6 to nested moves.
verification_level: WRITTEN. R6 is an elementary written proof, using the named-import size fact 330 | |B| only in orientation beta. R7 is a conditional implication whose hypothesis is an open conjecture. Neither is independently reviewed, formally checked or novelty-cleared.
